questions.ask: Will NIFTY be higher on {date} than today?
questions.plain: Will NIFTY be higher in about a month (20 trading days) than today?
questions.why: The basic call every investor wants: will the market be up or down a month from now.
questions.yes_when: NIFTY’s close 20 trading days later is above today’s close.

questions.ask: Will NIFTY move 3% or more, up or down, by {date}?
questions.plain: Will NIFTY move 3% or more, up or down, in about a month?
questions.why: Big moves decide whether options pay off: buyers need them, sellers fear them.
questions.yes_when: NIFTY’s close 20 trading days later is at least 3% away from today’s, either way.

questions.ask: Will NIFTY’s daily ups and downs be bigger up to {date} than over the last month?
questions.plain: Will NIFTY’s daily ups and downs be bigger over the next month than over the last month?
questions.why: A choppier market means bigger daily swings: more risk, and stop-losses hit more often.
questions.yes_when: NIFTY’s day-to-day swings over the next 20 trading days are bigger than over the last 20.

questions.ask: Will India VIX, the market’s fear gauge, be higher on {date} than today?
questions.plain: Will India VIX, the market’s fear gauge, be higher in two weeks (10 trading days) than today?
questions.why: India VIX measures how nervous traders are. Rising fear often comes with falling prices and dearer options.
questions.yes_when: India VIX’s close 10 trading days later is above today’s close.

questions.ask: Will NIFTY move less up to {date} than today’s option prices expect?
questions.plain: Will NIFTY move less over the next month than today’s option prices expect?
questions.why: Option prices carry the market’s own guess of how much NIFTY will move. This asks whether that guess is too high.
questions.yes_when: NIFTY’s swings over the next 20 trading days are smaller than the swing today’s 30-day option prices imply.
questions.said_yes: the market would be calmer than option prices expected
questions.said_no: the market would move more than option prices expected

yardsticks.name: Option prices
yardsticks.plain: The chance hidden in today’s NIFTY option prices. Option prices include a premium for risk, so this is the market’s price, not a true real-world chance.
yardsticks.label: risk-neutral

yardsticks.name: Past average
yardsticks.plain: How often the answer was yes over the last 3 years (750 trading days). A family must beat this to show it knows something more.

yardsticks.name: Simple formula
yardsticks.plain: A small textbook formula on recent swings (or on the fear gauge), refitted once a month.

rules.review: the first scheduled review, after 6 months of the three families paper trading together

standing: Profit decides which family trades. Prediction scores only show who reads the market best; a family never gets to trade because it predicts well.
